title: Security & Deployment Decision Criteria - LatticeWorks
summary: Initial security posture intake to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment paths. Customer prioritized SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, customer-managed KMS (BYOK), RBAC granularity, audit log streaming to SIEM, and retention/deletion controls. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 report, ISO scope, KMS runbook, SAML metadata, and schedule technical deep-dive with infra team next week.
topics: SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence and scope
Audit logs, retention, and SIEM export options
Encryption at rest/in transit and BYOK/HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Data retention, deletion, and PII handling
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya, Luis, Anika (Redwood) | Sara, Mark, Ellen, Rajiv, Jules (LatticeWorks)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll go over security and deployment criteria for LatticeWorks. Quick intros?
[00:12] Sara (LatticeWorks): Hi, I'm Sara, head of security at LatticeWorks. We're looking at inference providers, Redwood's on our short list.
[00:18] Mark (CTO): Mark here, CTO, mostly interested in performance and the data residency side.
[00:22] Luis (Redwood SE): Luis from Redwood engineering - I'll cover technical bits like KMS, audit logs and deployment topologies.
[00:30] Ellen (Eng mgr): Ellen, I'll be running the POC if we go ahead.
[00:34] Rajiv (Infra): Rajiv, infra lead, networking and compliance questions.
[00:38] Jules (Legal): Jules from legal for any contract/retention questions.
[00:45] Maya: Great — high level, are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private? What triggers each path?
[00:52] Sara: We're leaning towards hosted for speed but security needs might push us to dedicated or private. We need to know exactly what evidence you have — SOC2 Type II, ISO — and what gaps remain.
[01:05] Luis: We are SOC2 Type II and maintain ISO27001 scope documents. We can share the SOC2 report under an NDA and the ISO certificate PDF. For dedicated/private, customers typically require a bit more data isolation and sometimes BYOK.
[01:22] Sara: BYOK is a must for us if any sensitive PII is stored. We want HSM-level keys and rotation controls.
[01:29] Luis: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/GCP KMS and bring-your-own-key flows. For on-prem customers we can integrate with an HSM or an enterprise KMS - the runbook differs slightly. Note: our hosted offering encrypts all datasets at rest with provider-managed KMS by default, but we have an opt-in for CMK.
[01:47] Rajiv: How is the key material stored when we do BYOK? Does Redwood ever have access to the plaintext key or only encrypted blobs?
[01:55] Luis: Good question. With BYOK we never persist plaintext. We support envelope encryption: you keep the root key in your KMS/HSM and Redwood holds ephemeral wrapped keys. We can provide architecture diagrams in the follow-up.
[02:10] Mark: On audit logs — we need all request metadata for 365 days, ability to export to our Splunk or S3 bucket, and immutability / tamper-evidence. What's your support?
[02:22] Anika (CSM): We stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3, and we also offer syslog/HTTP forwarders for SIEM. Retention windows are configurable per account; hosted defaults are 90 days, dedicated can be extended. For immutability, we advise S3 object lock or sending to your SIEM with WORM settings.
[02:40] Sara: Are there any fields redacted by default in logs? We need full request/response headers for security investigations.
[02:47] Luis: By default we mask tokens and secrets, and we redact documented sensitive fields (credit_card, ssn patterns) in logs. For POCs and enterprise contracts we can enable a mode that retains raw transcript/logs under a higher-security profile if you agree to retention and encryption controls.
[03:05] Jules (Legal): Need to flag data retention and deletion for the contract. Does Redwood support on-demand deletion and proof of deletion?
[03:12] Maya: Yes — we have deletion APIs for data and we can provide deletion certificates for the committed deletion of customer data. We also support retention policies (30/90/365) and the ability to opt out of log retention for specific routes.
[03:26] Ellen: For the POC, we need to test with realistic payloads; is there a way to keep POC data isolated and ensure it isn't used for model training or telemetry?
[03:35] Luis: We don't train models on customer data. Telemetry is used for performance and health, but we can turn off certain telemetry and isolate POC projects in a dedicated namespace. We'll put that in the runbook.
[03:47] Mark: SSO — we use Okta and Azure AD, SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. How tight is the RBAC? We need least privilege and separation of duties.
[03:58] Luis: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC supports role templates (admin/developer/viewer) and you can create custom roles with scoped permissions (model deploy, billing view, audit read, key management). We also integrate with SCIM groups so you can map identity groups to roles.
[04:18] Sara: Do you provide MFA enforcement via SSO or do we manage that on Okta side?
[04:22] Maya: MFA is enforced at the IdP level; Redwood defers to the configured SAML provider for auth policies. We surface SSO session length and SAML metadata in the console.
[04:31] Rajiv: Network ingress — private deployment must support VPC peering, private link, or on-prem firewalled endpoints.
[04:40] Luis: For private we can run in your VPC, offer private endpoints, and peering. Dedicated can be isolated hardware with a private network tie-in. Hosted can use PrivateLink / peered routes with egress controls but it depends on region. We'll map options for your cloud provider.
[04:58] Ellen: Any limitations on model sizes or throughput in private/on-prem? Our models are ~13B with heavy KV caches.
[05:06] Luis: Runtime supports up to 70B in various quantizations, but throughput depends on instance type. For heavy KV cache we can tune cache sizes and allocate dedicated pools. That's part of the performance-run we'll do in the POC.
[05:20] Mark: Compliance evidence — can you share recent penetration test results and vulnerability scanning cadence?
[05:26] Luis: We perform quarterly vulnerability scans and annual third-party pentests; we can share summaries and remediation timelines. Full pentest reports require NDA and usually redactions, but we share key findings and mitigations.
[05:40] Sara: What about ISO scope — does it include the control plane for hosted services? We need to know which services are in-scope.
[05:47] Maya: We will share the ISO27001 scope document. For hosted, the service control plane and infra are typically in scope; we will call out exceptions if any.
[05:56] Jules: Contracts — retention, e-discovery hold and data subject requests. How fast can you respond?
[06:02] Anika: We aim for 72-hour SLA for access to records for DSARs and we can commit to longer timelines in enterprise agreements.
[06:10] Sara: Are there any known single-tenant options to meet strict data residency?
[06:15] Luis: Yes — private deployment or dedicated isolated clusters in a region. For strict residency we recommend private deployment in your cloud region or on-prem package.
[06:24] Mark: Competitors — just to be frank — we're also talking to A and B (Automata? Mistral? other infra vendors). Would Redwood support a side-by-side latency/cost benchmark?
[06:35] Maya: Absolutely — we typically run side-by-side benches. For the POC we'll provision a small dedicated pool and run identical workloads. We'll instrument cost and latency breakdowns.
[06:45] Sara: One last — audit trail tamper evidence: do you support signed logs?
[06:49] Luis: We can provide signed log attestations and integrate with your key management to sign log bundles, or send to an append-only store. We'll include options in the follow-up.
[06:59] Maya: Ok let's pause there. High level next steps — we'll send SOC2 under NDA, ISO certs, SAML metadata template, KMS runbook, and a POC proposal.
[07:10] Jules: Need to review data processing addendum and retention terms.
[07:15] Ellen: I'll coordinate POC test cases with Luis.
[07:19] Mark: Can we schedule the deep technical run on Tuesday next week?
[07:22] Maya: Yes, we'll propose slots. Thanks everyone.
[07:27] Sara: Thanks.
[07:30] [call ends — 52:01]
